title: Leeds reach FA Cup quarter-finals with win over Norwich: How this shapes the rest of their season
content:
Leeds United reached the FA Cup quarter-finals for the first time in 23 years with a 3-0 win over Norwich City at Elland Road on Sunday.

First-half goals from Sean Longstaff and Gabriel Gudmundsson and a second-half effort from Joel Piroe secured victory for Leeds against Daniel Farke’s former side, ensuring the club’s progress to last eight of the competition for the first time since 2003.

Leeds thought they had opened the scoring inside 20 minutes as Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw rushed out and failed to deal with a long ball, leaving Lukas Nmecha to stroke into an empty net. Following a video assistant referee (VAR) intervention, however, the goal was disallowed after Wilfried Gnonto was judged to have handled the ball in the buildup.

The Premier League side did take the lead shortly after the half-hour mark, Gudmundsson providing the delivery from the left and Longstaff controlling, swivelling and finishing superbly.

Leeds doubled their advantage two minutes before half time, Gudmundsson again involved as he finished from close range after Norwich were unable to clear Dan James’ low cross. The goal marked Gudmundsson’s first for the club since his summer move from Lille.

Piroe added Leeds’ third in the 85th minute, finishing first time into the bottom left corner for his first goal of the season after being played in by Nmecha.

Leeds will learn their quarter-final opponent in Monday’s draw, as they attempt to reach the FA Cup semi-finals for the first time since 1987.

Ahead of Leeds’ match against Norwich, Farke spoke of his desire to continue their progression in the tournament, although caveated that statement with the importance of his squad staying fit and avoiding injuries.

In a recent survey on The Athletic, more than 90 per cent of Leeds supporters said the FA Cup is still important to them, with just shy of 70 per cent of them saying they would rather watch their side lift the FA Cup than qualify for the Champions League.

Although this is restricted to Leeds fans who subscribe to The Athletic, it does clearly show — by a considerable margin — that staying in the FA Cup matters, so to have lost to Norwich this afternoon would have been a considerable blow.

But as it is, Farke’s side progressed convincingly into the quarter-finals for the first time since the 2002-03 season, where they were then knocked out by Sheffield United.

Their foray into the latter stages of this season’s FA Cup comes at the same time as they are engulfed in a Premier League relegation battle.

Sitting three points above 18th-placed West Ham United, and having not won in the league since the beginning of February, their top-flight safety is going to be determined over the course of the final nine games.

Some may view the FA Cup as an unnecessary distraction when set against ensuring their Premier League status, but beating Norwich should remind the squad what winning feels like ahead of next weekend’s match against Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park.

Leeds are now just one more FA Cup win away from a semi-final at Wembley Stadium and, as Palace proved by winning the competition last season, the cup favourites don’t always have their own way in the latter stages.
